newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli FM sees Netanyahu-Arafat summit this week.
newsitem.headline: Israeli FM sees Netanyahu-Arafat summit this week.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said on Monday a summit between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat would probably take place this week.
Levy told Israel Radio a summit "was expected". Asked if it would take place this week, he said: "I think so."

Netanyahu spoke by phone with Arafat on Sunday for the first time since Palestinians severed contacts over the Jewish state's decision to build a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem and other moves.
Netanyahu said he hoped the conversation, held during a visit to Israel by Jordan's King Hussein, would put Israel's dialogue with the Palestinians on a new footing.
But he also vowed Israel would break ground this week for the new settlement which Palestinians have said could trigger widespread unrest.
Israel claims all of Jerusalem as its capital. Palestinians view East Jerusalem, which Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war, as the capital of their future state.
